# Hooks audit: don't add the ruff hook; the real gap is that your existing checks may not be running

**Sizing: off** (default setting; no `time_units` is configured).

## Your proposed hook

**I'd recommend against it.** There are two reasons.

1. **A PostToolUse hook can't stop Claude from saving badly formatted code.** It fires after the edit is already on disk. I checked the hooks docs today: an exit code of 2 there only shows its error output to Claude, and it undoes nothing. Running `ruff check` after every edit also sends lint findings to the model on half-finished code, which is the placement this skill's rules forbid. Lint checks belong in a git pre-commit hook or CI.
2. **Both checks already exist:**
   - `.pre-commit-config.yaml` runs `ruff` and `ruff-format` (pinned to v0.6.9).
   - `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `ruff format --check .` and `ruff check .`.

A narrower version that only runs `ruff format` once per batch of edits and tells the model nothing would be acceptable in principle. I still rejected it because I couldn't measure anything: ruff isn't installed here, and the sandbox blocked downloading it, so I have no timing and no count of files ruff would actually change. It would also make hand-written edits fail when the formatter has already changed the text they expect. It's worth revisiting only if, once ruff is installed, it would reformat at least 5% of files and takes 1 second or less per run.

## Verdicts

| # | ID | Candidate | Verdict | Why |
|---|----|-----------|---------|-----|
| 1 | h1 | PostToolUse ruff format + check per edit (your proposal) | REJECT | Can't block; already in pre-commit and CI; lint findings per edit is the wrong place |
| 2 | h2 | Format once per batch, silently | REJECT | Already covered; no measurements possible (ruff missing) |
| 3 | h3 | Session-start check that pre-commit is installed | REJECT | A one-time setup step doesn't need a hook that runs every session |
| 4 | h4 | Block reads/writes of `.env` and secret files | REJECT | All 6 of 13 commits mentioning "secret" were dependency bumps for `secrets-manager-client`, not leaks; there's no `.env` file |
| 5 | h5 | Run pytest before Claude ends a turn | REJECT | CI already runs pytest; 1 of 13 commits mentions tests, and it adds a test rather than fixing a failure |
| 6 | h6 | Block force-push / pushes to main | REJECT | No force-pushes or reverts in history; every commit goes to main, so this would block normal work |

The pass/reject check ran in a separate subagent that hadn't seen me propose the candidates, so it wasn't judging its own ideas. It agreed with all six rejections.

**Events I looked at:** PostToolUse, PostToolBatch, PreToolUse, SessionStart, Setup and Stop. I ruled out the other 27 documented events because nothing in this repo touches them (sub-agents, tasks, worktrees, compaction, model switching, elicitation, file and config changes).

## The real gap: nothing may actually be enforcing these checks

This isn't a Claude Code hook problem, so it's outside this audit's categories, but it's what matters:

- **Pre-commit is configured but not installed in this clone.** `.git/hooks` has only the `.sample` files, and neither `pre-commit` nor `ruff` is on PATH. Fix it once with `pre-commit install` and add that step to CLAUDE.md.
- **CI only runs on pull requests** (`on: [pull_request]`), but all 13 commits are on `main` with no merge commits. If you push directly to main, CI has never checked any of this. Run `gh pr list --state all` to confirm, then consider adding `push: branches: [main]`. I couldn't check this myself.
- **The ruff versions can differ.** CI runs `pip install ruff` with no version, while pre-commit pins v0.6.9. Different versions can format differently, so code that passes pre-commit could fail CI's format check. Pin the version in CI, or have CI run `pre-commit run --all-files`.

## Caveats

- Several files were masked by the sandbox, so a hook or permission rule defined there would be invisible to me: `.claude/settings.local.json`, `.claude/hooks`, `.claude/skills`, `.claude/agents`, `.mcp.json` and your user settings. The automated inventory counts these as unreadable, not zero. My own read of the tracked files agrees: the project `settings.json` has no hooks, only two permission allow rules.
- With 13 commits, the commit-history numbers are thin evidence either way.

## Overall

Formatting, linting and tests are all covered on paper, and the amount of automation fits a repo this small. The weakness is that the local hooks aren't installed and CI may never run on direct pushes, so fix those rather than adding Claude Code hooks. Nothing passed, so there's nothing for you to pick.
